_about: Nearby stars for the parallax experiment (docs/PARALLAX_PLAN.md, 2026-11-20). Gaia DR3 values at epoch 2016.0; positions in degrees, parallax and proper motions in mas and mas/yr. 'plan' is what `parallax add <key>` writes on the queue row. 'refs' names the committed Gaia reference file under configs/parallax_refs/. Exposures follow the saturation rule photometry/lightcurve.py measured (G 13.5 saturates at 300 s in L): a quarter of the saturating time, R passband taken as 2.5 x L.

stars.name: Ross 248
stars.season: evenings November to January and mornings from July; the parallax factor peaks mid-December (dusk) and mid-June (dawn)
stars.why: The best match to this camera and site: unsaturated at 10 s in R, 800 Gaia stars to G 17.5 within 15', transits 2 degrees from the zenith, observable tonight and on both sides of the year. 10.3 light years; in about 36,000 years it will be the nearest star to the Sun.

stars.name: Wolf 359
stars.season: mornings from November, evenings by March, gone in May; the parallax factor peaks late November (dawn) and late May (dusk)
stars.why: The largest parallax this site can reach (7.9 light years, the fifth nearest system) and 4.7 arcseconds a year of proper motion, 18 pixels. Transits 55 degrees up in the south, above the low southern tree line. A thin field (126 Gaia stars to G 17.5 within 15'), so the plate uses second order only when it can.

stars.name: Barnard's Star
stars.season: mornings from March, evenings June to July; one side of the parallax ellipse only from this site
stars.why: The largest parallax of any star and 10.4 arcseconds a year of proper motion (40 pixels), but it rises in March and this site sees only one side of its year, so the parallax separates from the motion at about 5 percent. Add it in March for the motion; needs 2 s frames.

stars.name: 61 Cygni
stars.season: evenings in November, mornings from June
stars.why: Bessel's star of 1838, the first parallax ever measured. At G 4.8 it saturates this camera in a tenth of a second, which leaves only the brightest reference stars in each frame; keep it as the story and not the measurement until a short-exposure test shows the centroids hold.

stars.name: Lalande 21185
stars.season: mornings from November, evenings to May
stars.why: Reserve: the fourth nearest system and nearly overhead, but at G 6.5 it needs half-second frames and a thin high-latitude field gives few references at that depth.

stars.name: Groombridge 34
stars.season: evenings November to January, mornings from July
stars.why: Reserve: a bright pair (the companion GJ 15 B at G 9.7 shares the parallax) overhead in autumn, 1 s frames.
